title: Work IQ: real-time Teams meeting transcripts for apps and agents
summary: The licensing field says the model is unpublished even though the cited documentation establishes consumption billing. The app-permissions note also needs to limit its no-review statement to programmatic grants: the admin UI requires confirmation.

claims.claim: Work IQ lets apps and agents, including organisation-built ones, receive Teams meeting or call transcripts while the meeting or call is in progress.
claims.quote: Work IQ lets agents and apps, including ones your organization builds, receive the transcript of a Teams meeting or call while it's in progress.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center path is Meetings > Meeting settings > Transcript API access > WorkIQ access.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings. Under Transcript API access, turn the WorkIQ access toggle On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -EnableWorkIQTranscriptAccess $true enables Work IQ transcript access.
claims.quote:
When set to true, agents and apps can access real-time transcripts through Work IQ.

Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -EnableWorkIQTranscriptAccess $true -Identity Global

claims.claim: The EnableWorkIQTranscriptAccess parameter requires the latest Teams PowerShell module.
claims.quote: This parameter requires the latest version of the Teams PowerShell module.

claims.claim: For an app registered in the tenant, its API permissions are at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > App registrations, and then select your client application (not your web API).
4. Select API permissions, then Add a permission and select My APIs in the sidebar.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants with clientId, consentType AllPrincipals, resourceId, and scope grants tenant-wide delegated consent.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/oauth2PermissionGrants

Request body
{
   "clientId": "00001111-aaaa-2222-bbbb-3333cccc4444",
   "consentType": "AllPrincipals",
   "resourceId": "a0a0a0a0-bbbb-cccc-dddd-e1e1e1e1e1e1",
   "scope": "User.Read.All Group.Read.All"
}

claims.claim: The App registrations consent route applies to applications developed and registered directly in the tenant.
claims.quote: You can grant tenant-wide admin consent from App registrations in the Microsoft Entra admin center for applications your organization develops and registers directly in your Microsoft Entra tenant.

claims.claim: The general Entra consent route grants permissions immediately without review.
claims.quote: The Grant admin consent for {your tenant} button allows an admin to grant admin consent to the permissions configured for the application. When you select the button, a dialog is shown requesting that you confirm the consent action.
claims.fix: Replace 'The grant takes effect immediately, without review.' with 'Permissions granted programmatically are not subject to review or confirmation and take effect immediately.' The programmatic-only qualification is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/grant-admin-consent.

claims.claim: For enterprise apps, the consent path is Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications > app > Security > Permissions.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications.
3. Enter the name of the existing application in the search box, and then select the application from the search results.
4. Select Permissions under Security.

claims.claim: The consent call must use the app's required resource and delegated scopes rather than treating the Microsoft Graph example scopes as Work IQ permissions.
claims.quote: In the following example, the resource API is Microsoft Graph of object ID ffffffff-eeee-dddd-cccc-bbbbbbbbbbb0. The Microsoft Graph API defines the delegated permissions, User.Read.All, and Group.Read.All.

claims.claim: The meeting policy's Recording & transcription section is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy> -AllowTranscription $true allows transcription under the specified policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity SalesMeetingPolicy -AllowTranscription $True

claims.claim: Allow AI in all meetings must be on for Work IQ real-time transcripts to flow.
claims.quote:
| Allow AI in all meetings | Work IQ access | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off | Off or On | No transcript is available. |
| On | Off | Work IQ requests are denied. Other AI experiences work as configured. |
| On | On | Agents and apps can receive the real-time transcript. |

claims.claim: The AllowTranscription meeting policy governs whether transcription is allowed in a user's meetings.
claims.quote: Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit.
